data_and_models: No ML in the shipped path: Firestore documents, scheduled triggers and platform speech synthesis. No patient data model, retention, consent or offline behaviour is described.
name: Medvoice
one_line: A medication assistant that removes reading from the loop: a nurse photographs the pill, and the patient's monitor stays silent until dose time, then shows that photo and speaks the instruction.

sections.accomplishments: A functional cloud-synced tool built from a phone, and the confirmation voice loop working end to end.
sections.challenges: A 24-hour pivot: the original entry was disqualified on a technicality and MedVoice was designed and coded in two days. Firebase integration on a phone screen demanded precision.
sections.how_we_built_it: HTML5/CSS3/JavaScript front end with Firebase Firestore for real-time sync and the Web Speech API for the voice-over; built entirely on a smartphone using mobile code editors and AI-assisted development.
sections.inspiration: From an ER nurse's view: elderly patients return with complications not because medicine is missing but because they cannot read the instructions, and low literacy plus declining vision turns a prescription into a guessing game.
sections.learned: Designing for accessibility changes the architecture (asynchronous JavaScript, real-time database shape) rather than decorating it.
sections.what_it_does: Nurse portal: photograph the actual pill, set a daily or weekly schedule. Patient monitor: a no-reading interface that wakes only at dose time, shows the specific pill's photo and speaks the instruction. A voice loop repeats until the patient confirms the dose. Real-time sync keeps the patient's device current.
sections.what_next: Patient files with medication and adherence history, a PWA so alerts survive the app being closed, a low-cost vibrating bracelet with a physical confirm button, and Iraqi-dialect voice models.

testing: No tests, no evaluation with patients, no adherence measurement described - the confirmation loop is asserted to work in the demo video only.
